pid_data.process_description: 100T-01 serves as a buffer between the existing process unit and the Hydrogen Production Unit (HPU), with a design capacity sized for five days of inventory at the HPU rated naphtha flow rate. Liquid naphtha is received from the existing process unit at the battery limit and routed to Naphtha Storage Tank 100T-01, then withdrawn from the tank and transferred through the parallel Naphtha Transfer Pumps 100P-01A and 100P-01B to the HPU. The tank is an internal-floating-roof naphtha storage tank intended to mitigate vapor loss and prevent formation of flammable vapor-air mixtures by use of nitrogen blanketing. The tank operates at 38 degC and 0.01 barg, with design limits of 43/-8 degC and 0.07/-0.06 barg. Pressure control is provided by PCV-0101 for nitrogen in-breathing and PCV-0102 for out-breathing to atmosphere at a safe location through an activated carbon canister. Secondary pressure/vacuum protection is provided by PVV-0102 and emergency fire relief by EH-0101. Liquid level instrumentation includes level transmitters, indicators, alarms, and safety interlocks: LSHH-0102 with IS-09 closes the inlet shutdown valve UV-0102 to prevent tank overfill, while LSLL-0102 with IS-10 stops the transfer pumps 100P-01A/B and closes the outlet shutdown valve UV-0102 to prevent pump dry running. Naphtha is supplied to the HPU at a nominal flow rate of 37 m3/h, equivalent to 24,496 kg/h at density 660 kg/m3. Pump minimum flow protection is provided by continuous recirculation of 8.6 m3/h, equivalent to 5,653 kg/h, through restriction orifice RO-0101 back to 100T-01. Discharge flow is monitored by FT-0101/FI-0101 with FY-0101 shown in the flow indication loop. PSV-0101 provides thermal relief for liquid trapped in transfer piping. Emergency interlock IS-28, initiated by hand switch HS-0101, performs total system isolation by closing the naphtha inlet and outlet shutdown valves and tripping the naphtha transfer pumps.
pid_data.intention: The system is designed to maintain a reliable, continuously available naphtha feed from storage to the Hydrogen Production Unit while buffering the HPU against disturbances, shutdowns, or outages in the upstream process unit. Naphtha Storage Tank 100T-01 is intended to operate at approximately 0.01 barg and 38 degC within design limits of 0.07/-0.06 barg and 43/-8 degC, and to provide five days of inventory at the normal HPU naphtha demand. Stable and safe tank operation is maintained by nitrogen blanketing through PCV-0101, controlled venting through PCV-0102 and activated carbon treatment, and independent pressure/vacuum and emergency relief devices. Inventory stability and equipment protection are achieved through high-high and low-low level interlocks that prevent overfilling, dry running, and uncontrolled inventory loss. The Naphtha Transfer Pumps 100P-01A/B are intended to deliver a constant HPU feed flow of 37 m3/h while maintaining minimum flow of 8.6 m3/h through RO-0101 for pump protection. Emergency isolation by IS-28 is intended to place the storage and transfer system in a safe shutdown condition by closing inlet and outlet UV-0102 valves and stopping the pumps, thereby limiting naphtha release, preventing unsafe operating states, and sustaining feed quality and continuity during normal operation.

connections.node: Naphtha Tank Storage (100T-01) with Naphtha Transfer Pump (100P-01A/B)
connections.node_boundary: Node starts at the naphtha inlet battery limit from the existing process unit and nitrogen/instrument-air utility boundaries, includes 100T-01 tank storage, tank pressure/level protection, pump suction and discharge piping, minimum-flow recycle, vent/relief/drain systems, and ends at the HPU battery limit, ATM safe-location vents, and OWS/CSS drain boundaries.
connections.from_id: Existing Process Unit / B/L and Utility Boundaries
connections.to_id: HPU / B/L, ATM Safe Location, OWS/CSS, and 100T-01 Recycle Return
connections.flow_direction: Naphtha flows from the existing process unit battery limit into 100T-01, then from 100T-01 through the outlet shutdown valve to the suction of parallel pumps 100P-01A/B. Pump discharge flows to the common header and onward to the HPU battery limit, while a minimum-flow branch recycles from the discharge header through RO-0101 back to 100T-01. Nitrogen flows into the tank vapor space for blanketing, and tank out-breathing/relief flows to ATM at a safe location. Drains flow to OWS/CSS as shown.
connections.context: Single user-defined HAZOP node covering naphtha receipt, storage, blanketing, transfer, recycle, venting, relief, and drainage. Supports HAZOP deviations including no/low/high naphtha flow to HPU, reverse flow from pumps or HPU, tank overfill, tank low-low level and pump dry running, high/low tank pressure, nitrogen failure, blocked vent, PSV/PVV lifting, excessive vapor emission, pump deadhead, insufficient minimum flow, line thermal expansion overpressure, drain misrouting, and emergency shutdown failure. Engineering metadata preserved: tank operating pressure 0.01 barg; design pressure 0.07/-0.06 barg; operating temperature 38 degC; design temperature 43/-8 degC; normal HPU feed 37 m3/h or 24,496 kg/h at density 660 kg/m3; minimum flow 8.6 m3/h or 5,653 kg/h; five-day inventory provision; PCV-0101 nitrogen in-breathing; PCV-0102 out-breathing via activated carbon canister; PVV-0102 and EH-0101 secondary/emergency relief; PSV-0101 thermal relief; IS-09 high-high level closes inlet UV-0102; IS-10 low-low level trips pumps and closes outlet UV-0102; IS-28 hand-switch ESD closes inlet/outlet UV-0102 and trips pumps.
